answer: Demand agreement across independent issuers: an identity counts only when credentials from unrelated domains — a bank, an employer, a civic registry — all vouch for the same agent, each checked through a prism of zero-knowledge proofs that hide the documents. A sybil farmer can counterfeit one issuer's stamp, but faking a consistent set across domains that never talk multiplies his cost, and a zephyr of cross-checks catches contradictions. The anchor is independence: one compromised issuer cannot mint an identity alone. The weakness is coverage: thin infrastructure locks honest people out.
